title: Real-Time PCR System
purpose: Performs thermal cycling for PCR while simultaneously monitoring fluorescent signal each cycle, enabling target detection and relative quantification (via cycle threshold, Ct) without opening the reaction vessel after amplification — reducing amplicon-contamination risk versus end-point/gel-based detection.
operatingPrinciple: Combines a precision thermal block (or similar rapid-cycling mechanism) with an integrated optical module that excites and reads fluorescence from probes/dyes in each well or capillary after every cycle, generating a real-time amplification curve per sample that the instrument's software analyzes against a defined threshold to determine each sample's cycle threshold (Ct) or, if failing to cross threshold, a negative/undetected result.
basicOperation: Include manufacturer- and assay-specified positive, negative (no-template), and, where applicable, internal control reactions in every run.
Verify plate/tube sealing to prevent evaporation and cross-contamination between wells during cycling.
Review the amplification curve shape (not just the Ct number) for each sample — an atypical curve shape can indicate a technical problem even when a Ct value is generated.
importantSettings: Cycling program (temperature/time per step, number of cycles) specific to the primer/probe set and assay
Fluorescence channel/dye selection matched to the probe(s) in use
calibration: Optical calibration per manufacturer schedule using certified calibration dyes/plates; every run's validity is additionally verified through its own built-in positive/negative controls, not calibration alone.
maintenance: Keep the optical block/lens clean per manufacturer schedule to avoid signal attenuation.
Verify thermal block temperature accuracy per the manufacturer's periodic verification schedule.

commonErrors.cause: Contamination — commonly amplicon carryover from a prior positive run, or reagent contamination
commonErrors.fix: Invalidate the run, investigate the contamination source per the laboratory's molecular contamination-control procedure, and repeat with fresh reagents/controls

commonErrors.problem: Positive control fails to amplify or amplifies late/atypically
commonErrors.cause: Reagent degradation, pipetting/setup error, or instrument malfunction
commonErrors.fix: Do not interpret patient results from this run; troubleshoot reagents/instrument and repeat

safety: Handle nucleic acid extracts and amplified product per the laboratory's molecular contamination-control and biosafety procedures.
Follow manufacturer decontamination guidance for any spill inside the instrument.
